title: telemetry-workbench-notes-metrics-heuristics
summary: Working notes for an internal workbench: lightweight rules-of-thumb for metric names, cardinality controls, trace sampling tiers, and a small-space dashboard layout to iterate on for token-serving runtime signals.
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a working scratchpad for the observability workbench — a compact set of heuristics and a candidate dashboard layout we can prototype quickly. It is intentionally pragmatic: mix of exact metric-name suggestions (so instrumenters have something to copy) and open questions where we need instrumentation/infra tradeoffs decided. Audience: eng-observability, runtime, SRE, and feature owners who will onboard telemetry for new inference features.

Context & goals (short):
- Goal 1: Capture high-signal runtime metrics for tokenized inference (latency percentiles, token throughput, batch sizes, kv-cache hit rate) with strict cardinality limits.
- Goal 2: End-to-end trace anchors for request routing / model fallback chains so we can map errors and tail latency to policies.
- Goal 3: A small home dashboard (5–8 panels) for oncall and rapid triage; separate deeper dashboards for postmortems and capacity planning.
- Goal 4: Telemetry must be cost-conscious: sampling, aggregation windows, and TTLs specified up front.

Quick metric lexicon (naming and labels):
- Use a consistent prefix: rwinf_ (short for redwood-inference) to make grep/alerts easy.
- Counters: suffix _total; Gauges: _gauge; Histograms/Summaries: _bucket/_sum/_count.
- Labels allowed (strict): service, model, deployment_tier (hosted|dedicated|private), region, route, outcome. No free-form user_id or tenant.

Suggested metrics (copy-paste friendly names + short definitions):
1) rwinf_request_total (counter) labels: {service, model, deployment_tier, region, route, outcome} — Ingested inference requests (a request may result in multiple generated tokens). outcome: success|fallback|rate_limited|error
2) rwinf_tokens_generated_total (counter) labels: {service, model, deployment_tier, region} — total generated tokens, useful for cost attribution and batching efficacy
3) rwinf_request_latency_ms_bucket/_sum/_count (histogram) labels: {service, model, deployment_tier, region, route} — latency observed from request start to first byte and separate histogram for end-to-end completion (see note on two histograms below)
4) rwinf_kv_cache_hit_ratio_gauge labels: {service, model, deployment_tier, region} — computed periodically (windowed) by infra agent, prefer gauge updated every 10s
5) rwinf_batch_size_histogram_bucket/_sum/_count labels: {service, model, deployment_tier} — distribution of batch sizes (key for batching tuning suggestions)
6) rwinf_failure_by_type_total labels: {service, model, region, failure_type} — failure_type values: OOM|TIMEOUT|INFER_ERR|CONNECTION|MODEL_MISMATCH
7) rwinf_queue_depth_gauge labels: {service, region, priority} — internal request queue depth for backpressure tuning
8) rwinf_rpc_retries_total labels: {service, region, rpc_type} — client->runtime retries, helps detect transient infra issues

Notes on two-latency histograms:
- We should emit two histograms for each route: latency_first_token (start->first_byte) and latency_tail_completion (start->last_byte). Many user-visible degradations map to first-token tail. Keep both but use different HWM retention for cost control.

Cardinality rules & enforcement:
- Max cardinality per metric: 1k unique time series recommended; soft enforcement at the instrumentation library layer.
- Reject or map unknown model strings to model=unmapped when encountering new models in < 30d. Use a periodic job to reconcile unmapped->proper label values.
- Route label should be coarse (e.g., embeddings|chat|completion|rerank), not full path.

Tracing: sampling tiers and what to capture
- Trace anchors: every request should carry a trace-id (B3/W3C).
- Default sampling: 0.5% global (to keep cost moderate).
- Tail-sampler: keep full traces for requests in latency p95+ during a short time window (5m) or flagged errors. Implementation: use light-weight span tags to mark first_token_latency and tokens_emitted; tail-sampler triggers when histogram bucket crosses threshold.
- Always sample 100% for synthetic canaries and for requests from canary deployments.
- Span design: keep spans shallow. Root span (request), stage spans (routing, cache_lookup, model_infer, postprocess), and at most one nested span for kernel_op if we need fine-grain GPU timing in rare debug mode.
- Trace payload limits: truncate child spans after 100 spans; do not capture full prompt or model weights in traces. Sensitive fields redacted; only lengths and hashes may be stored.

Dashboard wireframe and panels (single small-pane dashboard):
We want a compact dashboard used by oncall to answer: is system healthy? where is cost or latency coming from?
Panel 1 (top-left): Request throughput (rwinf_request_total rate) broken down by deployment_tier and region — stacked area
Panel 2 (top-right): First-token p50/p95/p99 (latency_first_token histogram derived) by route — heatmap or small multiples
Panel 3 (middle-left): Batch size distribution (histogram) and avg batch size trend — shows batching efficiency
Panel 4 (middle-right): KV cache hit ratio trend and 1h windowed average — critical for short-context workloads
Panel 5 (bottom-left): Failure rates (rwinf_failure_by_type_total / rwinf_request_total) and top failure_type — bar chart + table of recent error samples (linked to trace ids)
Panel 6 (bottom-right): Admission/queue depth + on-deck capacity indicators (rwinf_queue_depth_gauge) — highlight saturation

Micro-alert ideas (cheap, high signal):
- Alert A: first_token_p95 > 500ms for >5m for any route in hosted tier AND requests_rate > 100/min — severity P1
- Alert B: kv_cache_hit_ratio drops > 20% absolute in 10m window for a given model — severity P2
- Alert C: batch_avg_size < 2 for 10m on a dedicated pool (suggests degen traffic) — severity P3
- Alert D: unmapped_model_count > 5 new names in 24h — action: signal instrumentation team to vet label explosion

Sampling / retention cost math (rough):
- Assume 100k reqs/min across hosted + dedicated, 0.5% trace sampling => 500 traces/min -> ~720k traces/day. At average compressed trace size 4KB => ~2.9GB/day ~90GB/month. If we raise to 5% it’s ~450GB/month. Use this to negotiate retention windows and storage tiers.
- Metrics retention: keep 1s-resolution metrics for 1d, 1m-resolution for 30d, 1h-resolution for 365d (configurable by metric class).

Synthetic canaries and signal quality tests:
- Create small canary traffic generator that emits deterministic prompts covering cold-starts, long-seq tails, and heavy-batched flows. Label canary requests with route=canary and sample 100% traces.
- Periodically run a short synthetic suite that measures a slice of p50/p95/p99 and kv-cache behavior; results get stored as separate timeseries (rwinf_synthetic_{suite}_result) so we can tie regressions to commits.

Open questions / tradeoffs (todo):
- How to practically enforce cardinality at the client library level without breaking existing telemetry? (Arjun to prototype safe mapper)
- What are SLO thresholds for first-token p95 by route? Product needs to own targets so we can map alerts.
- Do we want to emit prompt-length quantiles as a metric? (high-card risk but useful) — propose bucketing lengths into 0-64,65-256,257-1024,>1024 bins.
- Do we centralize model->family mapping in a single service to avoid label churn? (Luca to draft service spec)
- Tracing cost: can we implement a local tail-sampler that only sends full traces to storage during suspicious windows and otherwise sends lightweight span summaries? Prototype idea: send span counts + failure flags always, full payload only on tail.

Action items / next steps:
- [Maya] Draft a lightweight instrumentation checklist with exact metric names and recommended buckets for histograms by 2026-01-10.
- [Arjun] Prototype a label-mapper middleware that collapses unknown models to unmapped for 2 weeks and emits an alert for owners, target 2-week spike test.
- [Luca] Sketch a micro-dashboard in Grafana using the panel list above; include small-multiples layout for top 3 routes. Due 2026-01-18.
- [Priya] Setup a canary generator job and ensure route=canary trace sampling at 100% for canaries; initial run by 2026-01-12.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc light: many of the heavy design decisions belong in the playbook page linked above. This file is meant to be the lab notebook for quick experiments and to reduce copy/paste friction for engineers instrumenting new routes.
- When in doubt, prefer low-cardinality, high-signal metrics. We can always add more after we see real traffic.
- Remember to add an example Prometheus exposition snippet to the instrumentation checklist (counter + histogram with exemplar trace_id).
